text:
Predicates:
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
WorksInLibrary(x) ::: x works in the library.
ComputerScienceDept(x) ::: x is from the computer science department.
PartTimeJob(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
TakesCourse(x, y) ::: x takes the course y.
InstructedBy(x, y) ::: x is instructed by y.
WorksInLab(x) ::: x works in the lab.
Premises:
¬∀x (Student(x) ∧ WorksInLibrary(x) → ComputerScienceDept(x)) ::: No students who work in the library are from the computer science department.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ PartTimeJob(x) offeredByUniversity(x) → WorksInLibrary(x)) ::: All students who have part-time jobs offered by the university are students who work in the library.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ TakesCourse(x, database) → ComputerScienceDept(x)) ::: All students who take the database course are from the computer science department.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ InstructedBy(x, david) → TakesCourse(x, database)) ::: All students instructed by professor David are taking the database course.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ WorksInLab(x) → InstructedBy(x, david)) ::: All students working in the lab are instructed by professor David.
WorksInLab(james) ∧ Student(james) ::: James is a student working in the lab.
¬(PartTimeJob(jack) offeredByUniversity(jack) ∨ WorksInLab(jack)) ::: Jack neither has a part-time job offered by the university nor works in the lab.
Conclusion:
¬PartTimeJob(james) offeredByUniversity(james) ::: James does not have a part-time job offered by the university.
